question: to the Commission Markéta Gregorová (Verts/ALE) Subject:

A growing share of products on the EU market rely on cloud control centres operated through mobile applications, including solar inverters, robotic vacuum cleaners, smart home devices and connected toys. Auditing every such product is neither feasible for Member States nor proportionate for manufacturers, and software updates may alter a product’s behaviour. A targeted, low-cost measure would address part of this gap. Manufacturers and importers could be required to document all application programming interfaces (APIs) and control server addresses used by a product, including those used by future software versions, in the declaration of conformity and to ensure the control server can be changed by the operator. Such a measure would expose hidden functions, allow control centres to be switched where a manufacturer becomes unreliable, keep products working after insolvency and enable third party integration across brands. 1.

Do existing instruments, such as the Cyber Resilience Act or delegated acts under the Radio Equipment Directive, already require disclosure of control server addresses and APIs? If not, will the Commission assess the introduction of such a requirement?
Will the Commission examine mandating control server portability to extend product lifespan and reduce lock-in?
How will the Commission address the risks posed by software updates that introduce new control endpoints after placement on the market?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (17.9.2026) The Cyber Resilience Act (CRA)1, applying in full from 11 December 2027, requires manufacturers of products with digital elements2 to keep up-to-date technical documentation at least during the product’s support period. That documentation shall include, where applicable, a description of the system architecture explaining how software components build on or feed into each other and integrate into the overall processing. This may include identifying relevant application programming interfaces (APIs) and control server addresses. Furthermore, where a product is substantially modified as defined in Article 3(30) of the CRA after placement on the market, it is required to undergo a new conformity assessment. The Radio Equipment Directive3 does not specifically require the manufacturer to disclose control server addresses and APIs. It requires manufacturers to draw up a technical documentation, which, where appropriate, should include versions of software or firmware affecting compliance with relevant essential requirements set out in that Directive. In the framework of the Ecodesign for Sustainable Products Regulation4 and the 2025-2030 Work Programme5, the Commission has been working on the ecodesign of servers and data storage products, as well as on addressing, where relevant, aspects linked to software, durability and upgradability. Finally, the proposed revision of the Cybersecurity Act6 puts forward a framework to address strategic Information and Communication Technologies (ICT) supply chain risks and monitor dependencies in several critical ICT supply chains including cloud services. Within this framework, a range of targeted and proportional derisking measures, also transparencyrelated, could be taken.
1 Regulation (EU) 2024/2847 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 23 October 2024 on horizontal
